name: Backstabbers
overview: Scripture reveals the painful reality of betrayal by those closest to us, as seen in Psalms 41:9 where a trusted friend turns against the psalmist, and in Matthew 26:14 where Judas Iscariot, one of Jesus’ own disciples, conspires with the chief priests. Such backstabbing is not merely external opposition but a deep personal wound, highlighted in Psalms 55:12 which contrasts enemies with the greater hurt caused by those familiar. Proverbs 16:28 warns that divisive individuals sow discord even among close friends, while Jeremiah 9:4 cautions believers to be vigilant, as betrayal can come from neighbors and brothers alike, emphasizing the need for wise discernment in relationships.
